page.layout: One page of text, one column of verse, with no margin notes. Running head centred at the top, page number top right. Above the second heading the first poem ends with its closing line. Then a centred heading "D. Opt. Max. S.", followed by a second poem in one column.

main_text.p: Aut indefessis adisse laboribus arcem, Qua pietas regnat, justitiaque decor. Quisquis Hiantaas[?] trahit in commercia Musas, Et nostro afflatum numine pectus habet, Nec falsi pravique tenax male transigit ævum: Huic pulcra aeternus laude paratur honos. Omnia mors abolet: sola est sine funere virtus, Effugit extremos ingeniumque rogos: Felicesque animae terrena mole soluta, Aeternum summo cum Jove numen habent: Nocte carent atra: diroque silentis averni Termine, quod Lapithae Pirythoúsque luunt. Ergo ter es felix, caelo dignissime Vates: Te beat aetherium pro pietate tuba: Nunc penitus vivis: te vastus Olympus & orbis Laudibus in sera posteritate vehent: Docta per ora virum volitas: nil morte peremptum est, Ossa nisi, & tenuis, quae tegit ossa, cutis. Vos etiam laudis decus immortalis, Amici, Quarite: sic pariter vita perennis erit: Nec lacrymis porro tumulos aspergite: quisque Carmina sed Vati, dona suprema, date, Dicat ut aspiciens olim monimenta viator Funeris: VRSINI mollitor ossa cubent.
main_text.head: D. Opt. Max. S.
main_text.p: VRSINVM dederas Vnum[?], Deus optime, nobis, Sufficeret nobis tua qui pene omnia solus, Siue homines ille humana ratione doceret, Artibus excultus cunctis: sive enim heus[?] illum Spiritus arcanos depromere pectore sensus Jusserat: & sacri quatientem lampada verbi, Discutere errorum nebulas: cuneosque ruentum Divinis fretum telis hinc inde luporum Rumpere tutantem Christi divinitus agnos. Ergo quid VRSINO properata morte peremto, Crediderim superesse gregi, qui sicut in uno[?] Cuncta habuit quondam, sic cuncta amisit in uno? Sic ego multa gemens & planctibus aera complens, Tum[?] Deus excelsa miseratus ab arce gementem, Qu[?]one modum lacrymis, inquit, Vobisque sibique

page.notes: Faint mirrored text from the other side (show-through) on the right margin is not transcribed. No marginal notes. Doubtful readings are marked [?]: "Hiantaas", "Vnum" (the first letter looks like a Greek-style Æ), "heus", "uno" (both occurrences), "Tum" (the first letter is unclear), "Qu...one" (the abbreviation is unclear). The printed "Quarite" and "Pirythoúsque" are copied as printed. The final line runs to the foot of the page and may continue on the next page.
